title: Verify main screen on device (adb screenshot) and no visual regression
description: Install debug build on the connected Pixel 8 Pro, adb screencap in RU locale with permissions pending, confirm no overlap, tappable notes/buttons work. Also check EN locale render via config or emulator-free reasoning. Attach findings to the epic.
design:
## Goal
Prove on a real device that the main screen has no overlapping elements after tefal2garmin-muc, with no visual or behavioral regression.

## Preconditions
- tefal2garmin-muc done (commit on main, not pushed); device: Pixel 8 Pro 39261FDJG004CJ; app locale RU; BP/hydration permissions NOT granted (worst case = longest notes).

## Implementation Checklist
- [ ] adb devices lists 39261FDJG004CJ (fail fast if not)
- [ ] ./gradlew assembleDebug && adb install -r app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk
- [ ] adb shell am start -n com.zamotkin.extrahealthgarmin/.MainActivity
- [ ] adb exec-out screencap -p > /tmp/ehg_after_ru.png - verify: title, status, buttons, both notes, no line-on-line overlap
- [ ] Scroll to bottom: adb shell input swipe 672 2400 672 800; /tmp/ehg_after_ru_bottom.png - hydrationNote fully readable, not clipped by gesture bar
- [ ] Tap test: input tap on bloodPressureNote -> Health Connect permission screen (screencap evidence), adb shell input keyevent 4 back, same for hydrationNote
- [ ] Buttons render per HC state; manual Sync Now completes (statusText/logcat -s MainViewModel)
- [ ] Record screenshots + verdict in this task

## Success Criteria (measurable)
- [ ] /tmp/ehg_after_ru.png and /tmp/ehg_after_ru_bottom.png exist and show every element fully readable, zero overlap
- [ ] Both notes tappable -> permission screen (screenshot evidence)
- [ ] EN locale: EN strings are strictly shorter than RU at the same scale - if RU scrolls/does not overlap, EN cannot be worse; either verify once via locale switch or record this reasoning explicitly
- [ ] No functional regression: Sync Now pass completes

## Edge Cases (SRE)
- If a sync is in flight during capture (progressBar visible) - keep that screenshot as bonus evidence of worst state
- If adb device disappears - retry once, then report blocker instead of stalling

## Anti-patterns
- Do NOT verify by reading XML only - device evidence mandatory
- Do NOT pass with "almost no" overlap

## Effort
1h
notes:
DEVIATION APPROVED BY ORCHESTRATOR: verify with a fresh assembleRelease build instead of debug - the phone holds the release-signed v2.1.0 and a debug install would require uninstall (wipes Garmin login/sync state). Release signature matches, adb install -r replaces in place, user data preserved.
VERIFIED ON DEVICE (Pixel 8 Pro 39261FDJG004CJ), fresh assembleRelease @196b584, adb install -r in place (Garmin login + sync state preserved, data untouched). VERDICT: PASS all criteria. (1) No overlap: two distinct UI states captured, zero text-on-text overlap — /tmp/ehg_after_ru.png (pre-settle: login+sync buttons side-by-side) and /tmp/ehg_current.png (settled: 'Garmin подключен' + full-width sync/backfill). BEFORE overlap reproduced in /tmp/ehg_screen.png (sync button over hydration note). (2) Bottom/scroll: /tmp/ehg_after_ru_bottom.png byte-identical to top — content fits viewport, uiautomator shows ScrollView scrollable=false bounds [0,151][1344,2920], hydration note ends y~1682, fully readable far above gesture bar; ScrollView+LinearLayout confirmed in activity_main.xml, scrolls whenever content overflows. (3) Taps: bloodPressureNote -> HC permission dialog (/tmp/ehg_bp_perm.png); hydrationNote -> HC permissions screen (/tmp/ehg_hyd_perm.png; same requestHcPermissions() handler MainActivity.kt:177-178, HC routed repeat request to its management view — HC anti-nag behavior, not a layout regression); clean return /tmp/ehg_back_check.png. (4) Crash check: adb logcat -s AndroidRuntime — NO FATAL EXCEPTION / ClassCastException (only shell uiautomator VM noise); MainActivity cast change safe. (5) Functional: manual sync completed (/tmp/ehg_after_sync.png, last-sync 14:10->14:15; MainViewModel: BP pass enabled uploaded=0 waiting=0 dropped=0, hydration pass enabled sent=0 queued=0; no errors). (6) EN locale criterion: EN strings strictly shorter than RU at same font scale; RU worst case fits with ~1300px margin so EN cannot be worse; no locale switch performed (device not mutated).

title: GitHub promotion: SEO-first README + repo metadata
description:
## Requirements (IMMUTABLE)
- Requirement 1: README.md is English, keyword-first (Health Connect / Garmin Connect / body composition sync), one H1, renders with zero broken images or badges
- Requirement 2: GitHub repo metadata set via gh: About <=120 chars keyword-first, 8-12 topic tags across purpose/stack/field classes (no 'app'/'kotlin'/'android' tags)
- Requirement 3: MIT LICENSE file exists at repo root (README license badge must resolve)
- Requirement 4: Real device screenshots + sync-flow GIF stored in docs/images/ and referenced with keyword-rich alt text
- Requirement 5: .github/ contains bug + feature issue templates, CONTRIBUTING.md, CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md
- Requirement 6: Social preview image (1280x640) uploaded to repo settings
- Requirement 7: No code changes; repo-only scope (per user decision)

## Success Criteria (MUST ALL BE TRUE)
- [ ] gh repo view shows non-empty description and >= 6 repositoryTopics
- [ ] README renders on GitHub: all badges resolve, all images load
- [ ] LICENSE file present at root
- [ ] .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE renders in GitHub new-issue flow
- [ ] Screenshots/GIF captured from real device via adb, committed in same commit as README references
- [ ] git status clean, changes committed in English with Co-Authored-By trailer

## Anti-Patterns (FORBIDDEN)
- NO keyword stuffing (readability first; natural keyword placement per 2026 SEO guides)
- NO star-count badge at the top (RepoRanker 2026: bad conversion signal)
- NO broken badge/image links in a committed README (trust + conversion killer)
- NO 'coming soon' features listed as existing (RepoRanker 2026 anti-pattern)
- NO topic tags 'app', 'kotlin', 'android' (too broad / auto-detected language)
- NO repo rename: 'extrahealthgarmin' brand stays; keywords go to About/README/headings
- NO scope creep into code changes, fastlane, or CI (user decision: repository only)

## Approach
SEO-first revamp of the existing README (structure already answers what/for-whom/how-to-install); add keyword-first H1+first paragraph, badge block (version/downloads/license/minSdk), screenshots+GIF section with alt text, Releases installation link, star CTA. Set metadata via gh CLI (already authenticated). Add missing LICENSE, .github templates, social preview.

## Architecture
- README.md (rewritten, English) - the landing page / main SEO asset
- LICENSE (MIT, root)
- docs/images/ (screenshots + GIF from device via adb)
- .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.md, feature_request.md; CONTRIBUTING.md; CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md
- GitHub-side settings (description, topics, social preview) via gh - not in git

## Design Rationale
### Problem
App releases exist (v2.0.0) but repo has empty About/topics, no LICENSE, no .github, and README lacks SEO positioning - invisible in GitHub internal search and Google.

### Research Findings
External: nakora.ai/blog/github-seo (topics >=6, About <120 chars, LLM visibility via Google); infrasity.com/blog/github-seo; reporanker.com/blog/github-readme-best-practices (no mission-statement-first, no star badge top); codemotion.com/magazine/dev-life/github-project (keyword-rich headings, alt text).

### Approaches Considered
1. SEO-first revamp (CHOSEN): keeps proven structure, max SEO gain, minimal risk
2. Full landing-page rewrite: rejected - loses developer precision, 'mission first' is an anti-pattern
3. Metadata-only: rejected - README is the main SEO asset per all 2026 guides

### Scope Boundaries
In: README, LICENSE, docs/images, .github templates, repo metadata, social preview
Out (never): code changes, fastlane, CI workflows, store listings (user decision: repository only)

## Design Discovery
### Key Decisions
| Question | Answer | Implication |
| Language | English README | RU locale lives in app only; README targets global search |
| Scope | Full: README+metadata+releases+ecosystem | All 6 components in scope |
| Distribution | GitHub Releases only | Installation section links v2.0.0 release APK |
| Visuals | Screenshots + GIF | I capture via adb; user grants device access |
| SEO focus | Sync queries + category + developer | Keywords: health connect garmin sync, body composition, FIT weight scale |
| Boundaries | Repository only | No fastlane/CI/store work |
| Approach | SEO-first revamp | Keep structure, inject SEO |

### Open Questions
- Exact device availability for screenshots (adb access timing)
- Whether release APK asset is attached to v2.0.0 (to verify Installation section link)

title: Task 2: On-device capture — run the runbook on the real M7, verify spec, settle the 38B-vs-16B key discrepancy
description: Owner: user with the physical device, assisted by Claude for Wireshark analysis. Execute docs/omron-protocol.md section 9 runbook; produce redacted [CAPTURE-1..8] evidence; update the spec discrepancy table and flip [UNVERIFIED-on-device] markers to verified or corrected.
design:
## Goal
docs/omron-protocol.md is promoted from v0.9 to v1.0 verified: the runbook (its section 9) is
executed against the real M7 Intelli IT, [CAPTURE-1..8] evidence exists (redacted), every
[UNVERIFIED-on-device] marker is flipped to either verified-with-capture or corrected-with-capture,
and discrepancy #1 (38-byte vs 16-byte key) is settled.

## Context
Completed tefal2garmin-525: spec v0.9 committed (docs/omron-protocol.md, commit bbef2fe),
derived from omblepy @ f323d5a. New protocol facts discovered while writing it (beyond the
original research): the unlock-characteristic key protocol (02/00/01 opcodes, 8200/8000/8100
responses), settings read @0x0010 vs write @0x0054, ring-buffer unread counter with 0x8000
reset, time-sync block format. These are sourced but NOT yet device-verified.

## Implementation
1. User: follow runbook sections 9.1-9.3 (enable snoop, pair via Omron Connect, take one
   measurement, sync, retrieve log). Blocked on: physical device + ~30 minutes.
2. User + Claude: Wireshark analysis per 9.4 — Claude guides filtering and frame extraction
   (adb pull or bugreport extraction can be done by Claude if the phone is connected).
3. Claude: settle discrepancy #1 by measuring the key-write payload length in [CAPTURE-3].
4. Claude: update docs/omron-protocol.md — bump status to v1.0 verified, fill the discrepancy
   table evidence column, flip markers, record any corrections in a "Capture Amendments"
   subsection of section 10.
5. Commit only the spec update + redacted screenshots under docs/images/omron-capture/
   (optional, only if fully redacted).

## Success Criteria
- [ ] All 5 checklist items of runbook step 10 answered with capture evidence
- [ ] Discrepancy #1 resolved: key payload measured as 16 or 38 bytes, spec updated accordingly
- [ ] Every [UNVERIFIED-on-device] marker in the spec resolved (verified or corrected); zero remain
- [ ] At least one real measurement decodes with section 6 layout and matches the M7 display value
- [ ] Spec bumped to v1.0; committed diff touches only docs (no logs, no key material — verify with git show --stat)

## Key Considerations (SRE review)
- The M7 can serve only one app: unpairing from Omron Connect is mandatory BEFORE our own
  BLE client (epic 2) ever connects; otherwise both apps fight over the registration.
- If capture shows ALRU diverges from hem-7361t.py (region variant risk), record the delta
  explicitly instead of silently patching — epic 2 constants depend on this doc.
- Never let the raw btsnoop log into the repo: it contains the pairing key and the BD address.

title: Task 1: Draft omron-protocol.md spec v0.9 from omblepy source + device capture runbook
description: Extract every protocol constant from omblepy (omblepy.py + deviceSpecific/hem-7361t.py) into docs/omron-protocol.md with source citations and [UNVERIFIED-on-device] markers; write a step-by-step btsnoop capture runbook for the real M7 Intelli IT
design:
## Goal
docs/omron-protocol.md exists as spec v0.9: every Omron M7 protocol constant extracted from omblepy source with source citations, marked [UNVERIFIED-on-device] where a real capture is still required, plus a runnable capture runbook so the device verification (task 2) is a pure follow-the-steps exercise.

## Effort Estimate
5-7 hours (study omblepy 1-2h, spec 2-3h, runbook 1h, self-review against checklist 1h).

## Implementation
1. Study reference source (full read, not just README). PIN every link to an immutable commit SHA
   (resolve https://github.com/userx14/omblepy branch main -> current HEAD sha; cite file paths
   with symbol/constant names, not bare line numbers — line numbers drift between commits):
   - omblepy.py — session framing, CRC algorithm, unlock/write-key flow, channel selection among
     the 4 RX/TX characteristics, bonding handling, retry/timeouts
   - deviceSpecific/hem-7361t.py — full record/settings config (already partially extracted:
     slots @0x0098/0x06D8, 100x16-byte records, bit offsets, settings addresses)
   - Cross-check the CRC algorithm against the write-up at
     https://reverse-engineering-ble-devices.readthedocs.io/ (docs/omron.md ref 1)
2. Write docs/omron-protocol.md IN ENGLISH (repo convention: commits/code/identifiers in English;
   runbook may add a Russian quick-start subsection for the user, clearly secondary).
   Sections:
   - Source baseline: pinned commit SHAs + access date + how to re-verify
   - GATT map: standard services (0x1800/0x1801/0x180A/0x180F/0x1805/0x1810) + proprietary
     service/unlock/RX/TX UUIDs
   - SMP bonding: Just Works + ECDH notes, GATT_INSUFFICIENT_AUTHENTICATION handling
   - Pairing key registration: exact bytes written via 01c0, target address, key length
     (16B per omblepy vs 38B per docs/omron.md — flag as OPEN, capture must settle)
   - Session protocol: start/read/write/end frames with byte layout diagrams and CRC pseudocode
   - EEPROM memory map: user slots, record count, settings block (read @0x0010, write @0x0054,
     unread bytes [0x00,0x10], time sync [0x2C,0x3C])
   - Record layout: 16-byte bit diagram (year+2000, month, day, hour, minute, second clamp 59,
     mov, ihb, pulse, dia, sys+25)
   - Discrepancy table: docs/omron.md claim vs omblepy finding vs resolution status vs evidence
   - Decision log: what epic 2 (tefal2garmin-xtg) implements, pending capture confirmations
   - Capture runbook (see step 3)
   Every constant gets a citation (file + symbol name + pinned SHA, or doc ref). Constants not
   derivable from source get [UNVERIFIED-on-device].
3. Capture runbook (section in the same doc), target reader: the user with the physical device,
   no developer background assumed:
   - Enable Developer Options -> Bluetooth HCI snoop log (path to toggle identical across OEMs;
     log FILE location varies: list paths for stock Android/Pixel, Samsung One UI, Xiaomi MIUI)
   - Unpair M7 from Omron Connect (device supports one app at a time — explain why)
   - Hold Bluetooth button 3-5s until -P-, pair via Omron Connect, sync readings
   - Pull log (adb pull; note the file may need a device reboot or BT toggle to be flushed)
   - Open in Wireshark, filter: btsmp (pairing), btatt contains 0100/01c0 (session), bdaddr ==
     <device mac>
   - Checklist of frames to find: SMP pairing, key write (01c0), session start (0000/len 8),
     reads (0100), end (0f00), 2A35 indications — with screenshot placeholders [CAPTURE-1..N]
   - Redaction note: strip pairing key bytes before sharing/committing; logs never enter git
4. Commit only the spec doc (no logs, no keys).

## Success Criteria
- [ ] docs/omron-protocol.md committed, English, with all sections above
- [ ] Citation completeness: every hex constant and every UUID in the spec body appears within a
      citation block (grep-style self-check: no bare 0x____/UUID strings outside code fences or
      citation context) — zero uncited constants
- [ ] All three known discrepancies (38B vs 16B key, 0x08 vs 0000, SFLOAT vs plain ints) present in
      the discrepancy table with current evidence status and owner of resolution (capture)
- [ ] Runbook criterion: contains >= 10 numbered steps, covers >= 3 OEM log paths, and each
      checklist item maps to a screenshot placeholder [CAPTURE-N]
- [ ] Source baseline section pins omblepy commit SHA(s) + access date
- [ ] No production Kotlin code added; no btsnoop logs or key material in the commit
      (verify: git show --stat lists only docs/omron-protocol.md)

## Key Considerations (ADDED BY SRE REVIEW)

**Reference drift**: omblepy main branch moves. Bare "file:line" citations rot within months.
MUST pin commit SHA and cite symbol names. Re-verify links at execution time; if a cited symbol
was renamed, note old->new name in the spec.

**Regional variant risk**: docs/omron.md targets HEM-7361T-ALRU (RU); omblepy device config is
hem-7361t.py possibly verified against a different regional variant. If any constant in the
device config looks RU-market-specific (e.g. language bytes), mark it [UNVERIFIED-on-device] even
though it is cited — region mismatch is a real failure mode for medical devices.

**Snoop log quirks**: on many OEMs the log is only flushed on BT toggle/reboot; on Android 12+
the file may live under /data/misc/bluetooth/logs (root) with a bugreport-only retrieval path.
Runbook MUST include the fallback: `adb bugreport` extraction. If neither path works for the
user's device, task 2 must say so explicitly instead of improvising.

**Empty-input equivalent (docs task)**: "no data" case = a constant omblepy does not define
(e.g. CRC polynomial if only implemented inline). Spec MUST list such gaps explicitly in a
"Known gaps" subsection — absence of a value is information, not an omission to paper over.

**docs/omron.md as source**: its images are base64 data URIs (formulas) — treat as prose claims
only; every numeric claim from it lands in the discrepancy table unless independently confirmed.

## Anti-Patterns (ADDED BY SRE REVIEW)
- ❌ NO bare file:line citations without a pinned commit SHA (rot)
- ❌ NO presenting omblepy-derived constants as device-verified — [UNVERIFIED-on-device] markers
  are mandatory wherever capture evidence is missing
- ❌ NO committing btsnoop logs, key bytes, or BD addresses tied to the user (privacy)
- ❌ NO leaving a Known-gaps subsection empty "because everything is covered" — list it explicitly
  as "none found" or enumerate the gaps

title: Task 4: OmronSession — pure JVM session orchestration over a Transport seam (unlock, settings, ring-buffer read plan, batch decode)
description: Hardware-free session logic: unlock-command payload builder, settings block cache + unread-counter reset plan, ring-buffer read-plan calculator, full readout sequence over an injectable Transport interface. Android BLE client (Task 5) will implement Transport.
design:
## Goal
`omron/protocol/OmronSession.kt` drives the complete EEPROM readout sequence per
docs/omron-protocol.md §3-§5 as pure JVM code over an injectable `OmronTransport` interface:
unlock -> session start -> settings read -> ring-buffer record reads -> unread-counter reset
write-back -> session end. Plus `UnlockCodec` (17-byte unlock-characteristic payloads) and
`ReadPlanCalculator` (ring-buffer geometry). All unit-tested with fake transports —
no BLE hardware, no Android types.

## Context
- Completed tefal2garmin-nl5 (commit 7dd905e): SessionFrameCodec (fixed start/end literals,
  read/write builders, parser with XOR-CRC + 8f00 status), RecordDecoder, OmronProtocol
  constants. Learnings: session start is a FIXED literal (count=magic 0x10); read size lives
  in the count field; write commands are the only data-carrying frames.
- Settings semantics from spec §5: read block @0x0010 (68 bytes, but only the two 8/16-byte
  sections are fetched), write-back @0x0054 + section offset; unread reset writes 0x8000.
- The Android BLE client (Task 5) implements OmronTransport; fake transports in tests.

## Implementation (TDD)
1. `omron/protocol/UnlockCodec.kt`:
   - programModeRequest() = `02 || 00*16` (17 bytes); programKey(key16) = `00 || key`;
     unlock(key16) = `01 || key`. Validate key length == 16.
   - Response classification: classify(responseBytes) -> ProgramModeEntered (8200) /
     KeyProgrammed (8000) / Unlocked (8100) / Unexpected(type). `[SRC]` omblepy writeNewUnlockKey / unlockWithUnlockKey.
2. `omron/protocol/ReadPlanCalculator.kt`:
   - data class ReadCommand(address: Int, size: Int)
   - planForUser(settings8Bytes: ByteArray, userIdx: Int): List<ReadCommand> — implements
     `calcRingBufferRecordReadLocations` exactly: lastWrittenSlot = high byte of field
     [2i:2i+2], unread = high byte of [2i+4:2i+6]; wrap-around case (slot < unread) yields
     two reads, else one.
   - resetUnreadCounters(settings8Bytes): ByteArray — both 16-bit fields per user set to
     0x8000, other bytes untouched.
3. `omron/protocol/OmronSession.kt`:
   - interface OmronTransport { suspend fun writeUnlock(payload: ByteArray): ByteArray;
     suspend fun writeCommand(frame: ByteArray): SessionFrameCodec.ParsedFrame }
     (chunking across TX/RX channels, retries, timeouts are the transport's job — spec §4.5).
   - suspend fun readOut(transport, key, userSlot: Int): List<BloodPressureReading> —
     strict order: unlock -> start -> read settings section [0x00,0x10) -> planForUser ->
     read RECORD_BYTE_SIZE blocks -> reset unread -> write settings back -> end -> verify
     end status == 0. Any step failure throws OmronSessionException; session end is attempted
     in a finally block (device left in a clean state).
   - decode: each 16-byte block through RecordDecoder; nulls (empty slots) skipped;
     RecordFormatException logged-and-skipped (decision log #6) — collect into result with a
     skippedCount field on the result object.
   - data class ReadOutResult(readings, skippedRecords: Int)
4. Tests: fake transport recording writes / serving canned responses.
   - happy path: full sequence byte-exact against hand-computed frames; settings readback
     frame carries reset 0x8000 and targets 0x0054 (not 0x0010!) — pin this address.
   - wrap-around plan: slot=3, unread=5 -> two reads with exact addresses/sizes.
   - non-wrap plan: slot=50, unread=2 -> one read at slot base + 48*16, size 32.
   - unlock failure (8100 mismatch) aborts before start; end status != 0 throws after read.
   - session end is attempted even when a mid-read CRC failure occurs (finally behavior).
   - empty ring (unread=0) -> no record reads, reset still written.

## Success Criteria
- [ ] 3 production files + OmronSessionException, zero Android imports (grep-verified)
- [ ] 3 test classes; all frame bytes in expectations hand-computed and cited to spec §
- [ ] ./gradlew testDebugUnitTest --tests "com.zamotkin.extrahealthgarmin.omron.*" passes
- [ ] Settings write-back address 0x0054 pinned by a dedicated test (spec discrepancy #7)

## Key Considerations (SRE review)
- The 0x0010-vs-0x0054 confusion is the single most likely silent-corruption bug: a test MUST
  assert the write-back frame's address field equals 0x0054 + section offset.
- finally-block endTransmission: without it a mid-read abort leaves the device session open
  and subsequent connections fail with 133 — the classic BLE swamp. Test this explicitly.
- userSlot validation: accept only 1 or 2; a 0/3 would silently read the wrong medical data
  (cross-user contamination — the exact risk the UI user-slot selector exists to prevent).
- Transport interface stays minimal (2 methods): chunking/retry policy from spec §4.5 is the
  Android client's concern; resist adding transport-level knobs here.
- No time sync in this task (spec §5.2): it is a write to the device clock — deliberately
  deferred to a later task; note it in the result KDoc.

title: Unify the two blood-pressure upload pipelines (post-merge debt)
description: After merging omron into main (28896cc) the app carries TWO BP->Garmin pipelines that do the same job from different sources: the Omron BLE one (Room -> BpSyncCoordinator -> GarminRepository.uploadBloodPressure -> FitBloodPressureFileBuilder, UploadResult contract, journal bp_upload_journal.json) and the Health Connect one from PR #7 (BloodPressureSync -> GarminBloodPressureRepository -> GarminUploadClient.uploadHcBloodPressure -> FitHcBloodPressureFileBuilder, tokens+throw contract, journal blood-pressure-sync.json). They were reconciled mechanically for the merge (renames + uploadFitBatch adaptation): both work, but the duplication is real debt - two FIT builders (omron's is the superset with user_profile_index), two journals, two upload contracts. title: Blood pressure data layer + FIT upload (direct sync only)
description: Room (omron-scoped), FitBloodPressureFileBuilder via com.garmin.fit, share-sheet export + direct Garmin upload reusing existing auth pipeline
design:
## Requirements (IMMUTABLE)
- Room (androidx.room) is added scoped to the Omron feature ONLY: entities BloodPressureRecordEntity (id, timestamp, sys, dia, pulse, mov, ihb, userSlot, sourceSyncState) and DAO with insert-ignore (dedup by timestamp+userSlot), query of unsynced records, and mark-synced. Existing JSON-based sync state (health/ SyncStateStore) is NOT touched.
- garmin/FitBloodPressureFileBuilder.kt encodes a list of BloodPressureReading into one valid FIT file: FileId message (type blood_pressure) + one BloodPressureMesg per record (timestamp field 253 as DateTime, systolic field 0 in mmHg, diastolic field 1, heartRate field 6, userProfileIndex field 9 mapped from userSlot USER1->0/USER2->1), correct header+data CRCs — mirroring garmin/FitWeightFileBuilder.kt.
- The ONLY output path is direct sync: the existing GarminRepository/GarminUploadClient upload pipeline is reused for blood-pressure FIT files (tokens + OAuth already exist in garmin/); a per-record journal (BP analog of UploadJournal) prevents re-uploads; failures stay retriable and are never journaled.
- Record source of truth until successful upload is Room (per docs/omron.md NFR); a record transitions new -> uploaded only after upload confirmation.
- LoginRequired from the Garmin auth layer surfaces exactly like the existing weight flow (login dialog, token refresh automatic thereafter).

## Success Criteria (MUST ALL BE TRUE)
- [ ] Generated .fit file passes Garmin FIT SDK validator round-trip (encode -> decode with com.garmin.fit listener) with all fields intact
- [ ] Unit tests: dedup insert, unsynced query, mark-synced, journal dedup, retry-after-failure (not journaled), FitBloodPressureFileBuilder field mapping + CRC
- [ ] Direct upload reuses existing auth; LoginRequired surfaces exactly like the weight flow
- [ ] Failed uploads leave records in retriable state in Room (verified by test)
- [ ] ./gradlew testDebugUnitTest passes

## Anti-Patterns (FORBIDDEN)
- ❌ NO CSV export path anywhere (reliability: doc explicitly rejects CSV; Garmin CSV import is silently lossy)
- ❌ NO local FIT export / share-sheet (ACTION_SEND, FileProvider) path (scope: direct upload only — explicit user decision 2026-10-15; add it later as a separate epic if ever needed)
- ❌ NO retrofitting Room into health/ or garmin/ packages (consistency: existing JSON state stays; Room is omron/-scoped)
- ❌ NO new Garmin auth flow (reuse GarminAuthClient/GarminTokenStore as-is)
- ❌ NO marking a record synced before upload confirmation (data-loss risk)
- ❌ NO hand-rolled FIT binary encoding outside com.garmin.fit (SDK computes CRCs; doc requires official SDK)

## Approach
Room for persistence + one output path: direct upload via the existing pipeline. FitBloodPressureFileBuilder mirrors FitWeightFileBuilder one package over. BP upload journal mirrors UploadJournal (timestamp-keyed JSON in filesDir).

## Architecture
- omron/data/BloodPressureDatabase.kt, BloodPressureRecordEntity.kt, BloodPressureDao.kt, OmronBpRepository.kt (dedup + sync-state transitions, never throws)
- garmin/FitBloodPressureFileBuilder.kt (garmin/ package: it is a FIT concern like FitWeightFileBuilder)
- garmin/BpUploadJournal.kt (mirrors UploadJournal)
- GarminRepository gains a blood-pressure upload entry point delegating to GarminUploadClient with the BP journal

## Design Rationale
### Problem
BLE-read records need durable storage and a Garmin-compatible output; the app already owns Garmin auth + FIT weight encoding, so BP reuses both.

### Research Findings
**Codebase:**
- garmin/FitWeightFileBuilder.kt — direct template for the BP builder
- data/GarminRepository.kt (GarminUploadOrchestrator) — upload flow to reuse
- CLAUDE.md: "No Room, no DataStore" is an existing convention — deliberately overridden for BP because 200-record history + sync-state transitions need relational queries the JSON state file is wrong for (recorded as key decision)

**External:**
- com.garmin:fit:21.176.0 already on classpath; BloodPressureMesg present (verified in cached jar)
- FIT blood_pressure message fields: 253 timestamp, 0 systolic, 1 diastolic, 2 meanArterial, 6 heartRate, 9 userProfileIndex (verified via FIT SDK source)

### Approaches Considered
#### 1. Room (omron-scoped) + direct upload only ✓
Chosen: doc NFR mandates Room as source of truth; reuse maximizes existing investment; single output path keeps the feature surface minimal (user decision 2026-10-15: no share-sheet export).
#### 2. Extend the JSON SyncStateStore with a BP list ❌
No relational query/dedup, unbounded file growth with 200-record history; fights the doc.
#### 3. Direct upload + share-sheet export as fallback ❌ (was original plan, rejected 2026-10-15)
Rejected per explicit user request: the app exists to sync directly to Garmin; tokens and the upload pipeline already work. Export can be added later as its own epic if a real need appears.

### Scope Boundaries
**In scope:** Room schema, BP FIT builder, direct upload via existing pipeline, BP journal.
**Out of scope (deferred/never):** share-sheet/local FIT export (deferred — separate future epic only on real need), UI (epic 4), WorkManager periodic BP sync (deferred), cloud backup, multiple Garmin user profiles.

### Open Questions
- Does Garmin's upload endpoint accept blood_pressure FIT files from the DI API (weight files work today)? — verified at first real upload; if rejected, escalate back to user (export path would become a new epic)
- userProfileIndex mapping USER1->0/USER2->1: verify Garmin Connect displays both — manual QA in epic 4

## Design Discovery (Reference Context)
### Key Decisions Made
| Question | Answer | Implication |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| Room vs JSON state (doc vs convention)? | Room, omron-scoped only | CLAUDE.md convention overridden, documented here |
| Direct upload or export only? | Direct upload ONLY — no share-sheet export (user decision 2026-10-15) | Single output path; export = future separate epic |
| Where does FitBloodPressureFileBuilder live? | garmin/ next to FitWeightFileBuilder | Consistency |

title: App redesign v3: unified Compose UI, BP sources (Omron/BLE-1810/Health Connect), settings reorg
description:
## Requirements (IMMUTABLE — validated with product owner 2026-10-25)

- R1. **Unified UI kit**: single Compose design system — EhgTheme: dynamic color on Android 12+
  with a health-brand fallback palette, full dark scheme, Material 3 2026 expressive styling —
  drives every screen; one activity; bottom navigation Home / Measurements / Settings.
- R2. **BP sources are first-class and pluggable**: BLE drivers (Omron M7 Intelli IT; standard
  BLE Blood Pressure Service 0x1810) and Health Connect, equal citizens in the connections
  list. Adding a source type = adding a driver/adapter + one registration, no core surgery.
- R3. **Add-source flow**: Settings → Connections → Add source: BLE scan → select → pair
  (Omron: 16-byte key + one-time user-slot pick; 0x1810: system bonding) or Health Connect
  permission grant. Saved sources are listed, removable, with a per-source detail card.
- R4. **Selected user only**: Omron records carry a user slot — picked once at pairing, shown
  read-only afterwards; filtering at ingestion/display/upload. Sources without user
  attribution (0x1810 without User ID, Health Connect) attribute all readings to the app
  owner (stated as an info line, nothing to configure).
- R5. **Per-source sync mode**: History (full device memory read, idempotent) vs Current
  (only new readings since the last successful read anchor; anchors never advance on failed
  reads). Rendered only for sources supporting both; Health Connect is Current-only.
- R6. **Measurements = one page**: day-grouped readings (SYS/DIA/pulse, upload status,
  source tag), source card with "Read now" + background autosync toggle, empty state.
- R7. **Settings rationally grouped**: Connections (sources), Garmin (sign in/out, status),
  Health Connect (permissions), About (version, diagnostics). Home = status + sync button
  only; all service functions live in Settings.
- R8. **BP gating**: the Measurements tab (and all BP UI) is visible only when at least one
  BP source is connected.
- R9. **Record operations**: view + delete (selective and all, with confirmation) in source
  detail; no editing, no manual entry.
- R10. **Quality**: EN+RU strings in sync; unit tests for all new logic; lint green;
  existing weigh-in/Garmin sync behavior unchanged.
- R11. **Verification staging** (product owner, 2026-10-25): real phone + real BP device
  connection happens only in the final verification task (.10); all prior tasks verify via
  unit tests, fakes and `assembleDebug`. No data migration: BP data is taken fresh from
  sources (destructive Room migration acceptable; legacy Omron preferences not migrated).
- R12. **Docs & GitHub texts** (product owner, 2026-10-25): all documentation and
  GitHub-facing texts are updated to v3 — README (features + fresh real-device screenshots),
  docs/ coherence, repo description and topic tags, social preview, release-notes draft —
  following epic 43u's SEO conventions (tasks .11-.12).

## Success Criteria

- [ ] SC1: MainActivity renders Compose setContent with the shared kit; no XML layout drives
  the main UI; OmronActivity removed.
- [ ] SC2: Source registry resolves `omron-ble`, `ble-standard-1810`, `health-connect`; a
  fake fourth type registers with no core changes (unit test).
- [ ] SC3: Add-source flow works end-to-end for all three source types.
- [ ] SC4: User filtering unit-tested for Omron (ingestion/display/upload); HC and 0x1810
  attribution is app-owner with no slot UI.
- [ ] SC5: History/Current modes unit-tested, including anchor-not-advanced-on-failure.
- [ ] SC6: Measurements tab gating unit-tested (hidden with zero sources).
- [ ] SC7: Settings groups complete per R7; Home slims to status + button.
- [ ] SC8: `./gradlew testDebugUnitTest` and `./gradlew lintDebug` green; EN/RU string keys
  identical.
- [ ] SC9: final on-device pass on real hardware: phone + Omron end-to-end; HC source;
  0x1810 verified on hardware or explicitly recorded as pending-hardware.

## Anti-Patterns (FORBIDDEN)

- ❌ NO second activity for BP (unity: single-activity Compose app).
- ❌ NO vendor-specific code outside the vendor driver/adapter (extensibility contract of R2).
- ❌ NO `android.bluetooth` imports outside BLE driver + transport packages.
- ❌ NO business logic in Composables — ViewModels own logic (testability).
- ❌ NO read-anchor advancement on failed/partial reads (data loss).
- ❌ NO TODO/stub implementations shipped in tasks (completeness).
- ❌ NO DI framework (repo convention: manual wiring).
- ❌ NO user-visible hardcoded strings; R.string with EN+RU in sync (localization).

## Approach (validated option A)

Single-activity Compose app; one `BpSource` seam behind BLE drivers and Health Connect;
existing ui/omron Compose code absorbed progressively; OmronActivity removed once its
screens are replaced. Implemented as 12 dependency-ordered tasks on branch `redesign`; real hardware enters only
in task .10; docs and GitHub-text sync close the epic out (.11-.12).

## Architecture

- `ui/kit/` — theme (EhgTheme) + shared components; `ui/navigation/` — AppRoot scaffold;
  `ui/screens/{home,measurements,settings,devices}/` — one ViewModel per screen, manual
  wiring, LiveData bridged like ui/omron today.
- `devices/` — vendor-neutral seam: `api/` (BpSource, source types, capabilities, read
  request/result), `SourceRegistry`, `store/ConnectedSourceStore` (atomic JSON
  `bp-sources.json`), `omron/OmronBleSource`, `ble1810/` (standard driver),
  `healthconnect/HcBpSource` (wraps existing BloodPressureSync pipeline).
- Existing packages untouched in their logic: `omron/protocol`, `omron/ble` (behind the
  adapter), `health/`, `garmin/`, `data/`.
- Room: `BloodPressureRecordEntity` gains `sourceId`; unique index (timestamp, userSlot,
  sourceId); destructive schema migration acceptable — BP data is re-read from sources, no
  legacy migration (product owner decision 2026-10-25); upload journal unchanged.

## Design Rationale

### Problem

Two UI stacks coexist (XML MainActivity 611 lines + programmatic login dialog vs full
Compose ui/omron with its own bottom nav); no shared theme; BP is Omron-only and lives in a
separate activity; the existing Health Connect BP sync is invisible; settings/service
functions clutter Home.

### Codebase findings (2026-10-25 investigation)

- MainActivity: XML + runtime-injected Garmin views (:230-263), programmatic login dialog
  state machine (:485); deep links via intent extras; standard launchMode stacks instances.
- ui/omron: full Compose M3 (Dashboard/Pairing/Settings screens, observeAsState pattern,
  navigation-compose 2.9.8) — raw material for the unified UI.
- Existing BP machinery to reuse: pairing key store, readNewRecords vs full-transfer,
  User1/User2 setting, autosync switch, delete with confirm.
- Compose BOM 2026.06.01 + material3 already configured; no custom theme exists.

### Key Decisions Made (Socratic rounds 2026-10-25)

| Question | Answer | Implication |
|---|---|---|
| Second BP device type? | Standard BLE 0x1810 + Google Health | Sources = BLE drivers + HC, all first-class |
| "Google health" meaning? | HC = source on par with BLE | BloodPressureSync promoted to a visible source |
| Selected user semantics? | Auto-detect where possible → read-only setting; explicit where not | Omron: one-time slot pick; HC/0x1810: app owner |
| Navigation? | 3 tabs, Measurements gated | Single activity, bottom nav |
| Sync modes? | Per-source setting | History/Current + anchors |
| Home content? | Status + button | No charts (YAGNI) |
| Theme? | Dynamic color + brand fallback | M3 dynamic on 12+ |
| BLE read automation? | Button + autosync toggle | Generalize Omron autosync |
| Record operations? | View + delete only | No manual entry/editing |
| Hardware verification? | Last stage only | Fakes/unit tests until final task .10 |
| Data migration? | Ignore — fresh start from sources | Destructive Room migration, no legacy prefs |
| Docs & GitHub texts? | Update all to v3 (README, screenshots, topics, social, release notes) | Tasks .11-.12 after the hardware pass |

### Approaches Considered

1. **Single app + BpSource seam** ✓ — chosen: meets unity, extensibility, HC-first-class.
2. **BLE-only driver seam, HC stays hidden** ❌ — rejected: contradicts the Google Health
   decision; gating of Measurements becomes inconsistent. DO NOT REVISIT.
3. **Restyle both activities with a shared kit** ❌ — rejected: split navigation remains,
   extensibility decorative. DO NOT REVISIT.

### Scope Boundaries

In: three source types, unified Compose UI, settings reorg, user filtering, sync modes,
measurements page, v3.0.0 version bump.
Out: Home analytics/charts; multi-profile app accounts; weight-scale BLE drivers; release
publishing (v3.0.0 notes are drafted in .11-.12, publishing itself is out); data migration
from the current Room DB / legacy Omron preferences (fresh start from sources); epics 8qt /
9dk (stay separate; done epic 43u's SEO conventions are inherited by .11-.12).

### Open Questions

- 0x1810 timestamps are flag-gated and often missing — device timestamp when present,
  read-time + fingerprint dedup otherwise. RESOLVED by research 2026-10-25 (folded into
  task .9): sentinel readings 0x07FF filtered, self-disconnect after transfer is normal,
  delete-after-transfer models exist, userID null/0xFF, verified device families A&D /
  Beurer / Omron Smart / boso / Silvercrest / Medisana.
- Omron autosync mechanism generalization for multi-source background reads (resolved in
  task .6).
- Is a real 0x1810 device available for the final verification pass? (resolved at task .10).

title: UI kit: shared Compose theme + components + app scaffold + Home migration
description:
## Goal

One shared Compose UI kit + app scaffold. MainActivity migrates from XML + programmatic views
(611 lines today) to Compose hosting bottom navigation (Home / Measurements / Settings).
This is a FAITHFUL migration — no functional reorganization (that is T7), no BP changes
(OmronActivity stays untouched until T3/T6 absorb it).

## Design

Current state (verified): two UI stacks coexist — MainActivity is XML/View-based
(`setContentView(R.layout.activity_main)`, runtime-injected Garmin views at MainActivity:230-263,
programmatic login AlertDialog at :485); ui/omron is full Compose M3. No shared theme exists
(only a lone default-purple token in colors.xml). Compose deps, BOM 2026.06.01 and
navigation-compose 2.9.8 are already in app/build.gradle.

- `ui/kit/theme/EhgTheme.kt` — Material 3 theme: dynamic color on Android 12+, full brand
  fallback palette (light + dark schemes; health-oriented teal/green tokens, not the default
  purple), expressive type scale. Single source of design tokens for the whole app.
- `ui/kit/components/` — shared components (Home uses them now, every later screen reuses):
  `SectionCard`, `StatusRow` (leading icon, label, value, trailing status chip),
  `SectionHeader`, `EhgButton` (primary/tonal), `EmptyState`, `LabeledValue`. No
  screen-specific logic inside kit components.
- `ui/navigation/AppRoot.kt` — Scaffold + NavigationBar (Home, Measurements, Settings) +
  NavHost. At this stage Measurements renders a minimal honest empty state ("connect a blood
  pressure source in Settings"); real gating on connected sources lands in T6.
- `ui/screens/home/HomeScreen.kt` — faithful Compose port of today's MainActivity content,
  wired to the existing MainViewModel via LiveData bridge (runtime-livedata + observeAsState,
  same pattern as ui/omron): header, HC status line (tap → permission screen / Play Store),
  progress + status text, last-sync + pending line, Sync now, Backfill (24h/7d/30d picker
  dialog), "Blood pressure (Omron)" entry button (kept until T6/T7), BP/hydration optional
  permission notes (tap to allow), Garmin connect button/label, privacy-policy dialog.
- Garmin login dialog → Compose AlertDialog (email/password → MFA field → inline error,
  resend-code neutral button) driven by the existing MainUiState login fields. Port the
  duplicate-emission guards (MainActivity:100-101) — don't regress them.
- `MainActivity` — AppCompatActivity + `setContent { EhgTheme { AppRoot() } }`,
  `enableEdgeToEdge()`, POST_NOTIFICATIONS request preserved, deep links preserved:
  `EXTRA_SHOW_GARMIN_LOGIN`, `EXTRA_HEALTH_PERMISSIONS_RATIONALE`, notification deep links.
  Set `launchMode="singleTop"` + onNewIntent dispatch so rationale aliases and notifications
  stop stacking duplicate activities (fixes today's standard-launchMode oddity).
- Delete `res/layout/activity_main.xml` and all findViewById/programmatic view code from
  MainActivity. ui/omron (OmronActivity etc.) stays untouched.
- Strings: reuse the existing 99 keys wherever text matches; add only genuinely new ones
  (nav labels, kit empty states); EN + RU kept in sync.

## Implementation Checklist

- [ ] EhgTheme (dynamic color + brand fallback + dark) applied at the app root
- [ ] Shared kit components in ui/kit/components
- [ ] AppRoot scaffold: NavigationBar with 3 destinations + NavHost
- [ ] HomeScreen faithful port (all sections above) wired to MainViewModel
- [ ] Compose login dialog (incl. MFA + resend + inline error), backfill picker, privacy dialog
- [ ] MainActivity setContent + edge-to-edge + singleTop/onNewIntent deep-link handling
- [ ] Delete activity_main.xml + programmatic view code
- [ ] Strings EN + RU for every new label
- [ ] `./gradlew assembleDebug` + `./gradlew testDebugUnitTest` green

## Success Criteria

- [ ] `grep -c findViewById app/src/main/java/com/zamotkin/extrahealthgarmin/MainActivity.kt` == 0
- [ ] `res/layout/activity_main.xml` deleted; `./gradlew assembleDebug` green
- [ ] Every Home interaction preserved: sync now, backfill (3 windows), HC status tap-through,
  Garmin connect + login incl. MFA/resend, BP/hydration notes tap-to-allow, Omron entry button
- [ ] Dark theme + dynamic color active via EhgTheme; no hardcoded colors in new code
- [ ] Deep links (login extra, rationale alias, notifications) do not stack activities
- [ ] `./gradlew testDebugUnitTest` green (existing MainViewModel tests unaffected)

## Key Considerations

- Login dialog is a state machine keyed off LiveData emissions with duplicate-emission guards —
  port the guards, or the dialog can flicker/reopen.
- statusText is deliberately overloaded today (Garmin upload + HC sync mapped onto one enum);
  keep that mapping as-is in this task.
- `hcSyncError` is never rendered today — keep rendering nothing (faithful migration).
- Edge-to-edge: apply status-bar insets to scroll content so the header isn't underlapped.
- Do not touch: OmronActivity, ui/omron screens, sync/aggregation/auth logic.

## Anti-patterns

- No new business logic in Composables — MainViewModel stays the logic owner.
- No hardcoded colors/typography/dimensions outside the theme.
- No TODOs, no stub implementations, no `!!`.

## Effort Estimate

8 hours

title: Final on-device verification: real phone + real BP device end-to-end
description:
## Goal

Final-stage verification on REAL hardware (product owner decision 2026-10-25): install on
the real phone, connect the real blood-pressure device(s), and exercise the flows
end-to-end. All prior tasks verified via fakes and unit tests — this task is where real
BLE, real bonding and a real Garmin account meet the new UI.

## Design

- Install the debug build on the connected phone (`./debug_setup.sh` or adb install).
- Walkthrough of every hardware-dependent epic criterion:
  - Add-source flow with the real Omron M7 Intelli IT: scan, 16-byte key pairing,
    one-time user-slot pick.
  - History read (full device memory) and Current read (new readings only) on the real
    device — no duplicates, no gaps.
  - Autosync toggle + manual "Read now".
  - Garmin upload of the selected user's readings (real account; verify in Garmin Connect).
  - Health Connect source: permission grant + incremental sync on the real phone.
  - Standard BLE 0x1810 device: IF one is available — full pairing/read verification; if
    not at hand, verify via the driver's fake-harness tests and record on-device 0x1810
    verification as pending-hardware (honest state, no silent skip).
- Deep links, notifications, dark mode, dynamic color checked on the real screen.
- Every finding becomes a fix: small fixes land directly here; structural ones become
  follow-up tasks in this epic.

## Implementation Checklist

- [ ] Build + install on the real phone
- [ ] Omron end-to-end: pair, slot pick, history read, current read, upload, autosync
- [ ] HC source end-to-end: grant, incremental sync
- [ ] 0x1810 end-to-end (or recorded as pending-hardware with fake-harness evidence)
- [ ] UI/UX walkthrough: dark mode, dynamic color, deep links, notifications
- [ ] Findings fixed or filed; evidence captured (screenshots, logcat lines)

## Success Criteria

- [ ] Real Omron device: full flow works — pair → read → Garmin shows the selected user's
  readings
- [ ] History and Current modes behave per spec on the real device (no duplicates, no gaps)
- [ ] HC source syncs on the real phone
- [ ] 0x1810: verified on hardware OR explicitly recorded as pending-hardware
- [ ] All findings closed (fixed or filed as tasks)
- [ ] `./gradlew testDebugUnitTest` still green after any fixes

## Key Considerations

- This task needs the physical devices at hand — coordinate with the owner; never mark a
  criterion verified without hardware evidence.
- Keep an evidence checklist per criterion (screenshot / logcat line / Garmin screenshot).

## Anti-Patterns

- No marking criteria verified without evidence.
- No TODOs, no stub implementations.

## Effort Estimate

4 hours (plus hardware availability)

title: Fix xlg.2 review: BpSource.read never-throw contract — guard keyProvider/syncPass
description:
## Goal

Fix the two NEEDS_FIX findings from the xlg.2 quality review (2026-10-25): `BpSource.read`
must honor its documented never-throw contract.

## Findings (from the review)

1. [major] devices/omron/OmronBleSource.kt:51 — `read()` calls `keyProvider()` unguarded.
   The production binding (OmronKeyStore.getOrCreate) throws IllegalStateException from
   KeystoreAesPairingKeyCrypto.encrypt on Keystore failure and IOException /
   IllegalStateException from FileKeyPersistence.save on first key generation. The
   pre-sources caller (OmronViewModel.startPass) wrapped this call in try/catch; the
   adapter dropped the guard.
2. [major] devices/healthconnect/HcBpSource.kt:46 — `read()` calls `syncPass()` unguarded.
   The production binding (facade.syncBloodPressure) can throw: HC provider IPC in
   canReadBloodPressure and IOException from FileBloodPressureStateStore.save. Every other
   caller of this pipeline wraps it (MainViewModel.kt:372/398, SyncWorker.kt:78).

## Fix

- Wrap both seam calls: catch exceptions → `SourceReadResult.Failed`; rethrow
  `CancellationException` (coroutines hygiene — follow the existing pattern at
  MainViewModel.kt:372).
- Unit tests with throwing fakes: keyProvider throwing IllegalStateException → Failed;
  syncPass throwing IOException → Failed; CancellationException propagates, not swallowed.

## Success Criteria

- [ ] Throwing-fake tests cover both adapters (Failed result, no exception escapes read())
- [ ] CancellationException rethrow tested
- [ ] `./gradlew testDebugUnitTest` green

title: BP source abstraction: registry, ConnectedSourceStore, Omron + Health Connect adapters, Room sourceId
description:
## Goal

Vendor-neutral blood-pressure SOURCE abstraction: one seam behind BLE drivers and Health
Connect. Omron and Health Connect become the first two source types; the standard BLE 0x1810
driver (task .9) plugs into the same seam later. No UI work here — abstraction, registry,
persistence, adapters, Room column.

## Design

New top-level package `devices/` (vendor-neutral seam; `omron/` stays vendor-specific):

- `devices/api/BpSource.kt` — the seam: `sourceTypeId: String`, `displayNameRes: Int`,
  `capabilities: SourceCapabilities` (userAttribution: SLOTS | NONE; supportedSyncModes:
  set of HISTORY/CURRENT; requiresPairingKey), read API:
  `suspend fun read(request: SourceReadRequest): SourceReadResult` (request: sync mode +
  optional user slot; result: readings + per-source counters).
- `devices/api/BpSourceType.kt` — factory per source type: BLE types create a source from a
  `DiscoveredBleDevice` (name, address, rssi); `health-connect` is a singleton type whose
  connect step is a permission grant, not a scan.
- `devices/SourceRegistry.kt` — resolves sourceTypeId → factory. Registered:
  `omron-ble`, `health-connect` (task .9 adds `ble-standard-1810`). Adding a type = one
  registration.
- `devices/store/ConnectedSourceStore.kt` — atomic JSON in filesDir (`bp-sources.json`),
  SyncStateStore pattern (temp + rename). `ConnectedSource`: id (UUID), sourceTypeId, name,
  address (BLE only), pairingKeyRef, userSlot (Omron only, nullable), syncMode (default
  HISTORY), lastReadAnchor (nullable), createdAt. Corrupt file => empty list + log, never
  crash.
- `devices/omron/OmronBleSource.kt` — adapter over the existing omron/ble stack
  (OmronBleClient etc. untouched): userAttribution SLOTS, modes HISTORY | CURRENT (full mode
  semantics land in task .5; this task maps the calls).
- `devices/healthconnect/HcBpSource.kt` — adapter over the existing health/BloodPressureSync
  pipeline (changes-token incremental reads): userAttribution NONE (phone owner),
  supportedSyncModes = CURRENT only; initial connect preserves today's backfill window.
- Room: `BloodPressureRecordEntity` gains `sourceId: String`; unique index becomes
  (timestamp, userSlot, sourceId). Schema version bump with DESTRUCTIVE migration — BP data
  is re-read from sources, legacy rows are not migrated (product owner decision 2026-10-25).
  `BpUploadJournal` composite key stays (timestamp, userSlot) — Garmin dedups per
  user+timestamp.
- Wiring: registry + store constructed in `HealthSyncWiring` (manual, no DI framework).

## Implementation Checklist

- [ ] devices/api interfaces + data classes (source, source type, capabilities, request/result)
- [ ] SourceRegistry with omron-ble + health-connect registered
- [ ] ConnectedSourceStore atomic persistence
- [ ] OmronBleSource adapter over omron/ble
- [ ] HcBpSource adapter over BloodPressureSync
- [ ] Room sourceId + destructive migration + DAO query updates
- [ ] HealthSyncWiring wiring
- [ ] Unit tests (see below)

## Success Criteria

- [ ] `SourceRegistryTest`: resolves omron-ble and health-connect; a fake third type
  registers and resolves with no core changes (proves SC2 extensibility)
- [ ] `ConnectedSourceStoreTest`: save/load roundtrip; corrupt file => empty list (not
  crash); atomic write leaves old file intact on failure
- [ ] `OmronBleSourceTest` / `HcBpSourceTest`: request/result mapping via faked seams; HC
  capabilities assert NONE attribution + CURRENT-only modes
- [ ] Room migration compiles; DAO tests updated for sourceId and green
- [ ] Existing BP pipelines keep working unchanged behind the seam
- [ ] `./gradlew testDebugUnitTest` green

## Key Considerations

- This is a refactor, not a behavior change: Omron reads and HC BloodPressureSync produce
  identical results through the seam.
- Store/registry never throw (gateway convention).
- BLE imports stay inside BLE source packages; `devices/api` must not import
  `android.bluetooth`.
- No hardware in this task: verify via fakes + unit tests; real BLE runs only in the final
  verification task (.10).

## Anti-Patterns

- No DI framework, no reflection-based plugin loading — plain map in SourceRegistry.
- No TODOs, no stub implementations, no `!!`.

## Effort Estimate

8 hours

title: Selected user only: one-time Omron slot pick (read-only), filtering at ingestion/display/upload
description:
## Goal

Selected-user semantics for BP data (epic R4): the Omron user slot is picked ONCE during
pairing and shown read-only afterwards; filtering at ingestion, display and upload. Sources
without user attribution (0x1810, Health Connect) attribute all readings to the app owner —
an info line, nothing to configure.

## Design

- Pairing flow (task .3 screens) asks "which device user are you?" exactly once for sources
  with `userAttribution == SLOTS`; the answer is stored in `ConnectedSource.userSlot` and
  displayed READ-ONLY in the source detail card ("Device user: A"). Changing the slot =
  remove + re-add the source (explicit, rare, no accidental re-filtering).
- Ingestion filter: Omron read results for non-selected slots are dropped before insert
  (other household members' data never enters the app's dataset).
- Display/upload filter: queries filter by sourceId + userSlot, so pre-existing rows from
  other slots (read before this feature) are excluded once a slot is chosen.
- No legacy migration: the slot is chosen fresh at pairing; the legacy Omron User1/User2
  preference (`SharedPreferencesOmronSettingsStore`) is not read (product owner: fresh
  start).
- NONE-attribution sources (HC, 0x1810): source detail shows an info line "All readings are
  attributed to the app owner"; no slot UI anywhere.

## Implementation Checklist

- [ ] One-time slot pick step in the pairing flow (SLOTS sources only)
- [ ] Read-only slot row in source detail (+ info line for NONE sources)
- [ ] Ingestion filter in the read→Room insert path
- [ ] Slot-filtered DAO queries + display/upload wiring
- [ ] Verify the legacy Omron preference is ignored (fresh start)
- [ ] Strings EN + RU
- [ ] Unit tests (see below)

## Success Criteria

- [ ] Ingestion test: fake source returns slots A and B, selected A => only A rows inserted
  (catches missing ingestion filter)
- [ ] Display/upload test: DB holds A and B rows, selected B => only B rows returned
  (catches filter applied at the wrong layer)
- [ ] Fresh-start test: no legacy preference is read; the slot comes from the pairing step
  only
- [ ] NONE-source test: no slot filtering, no slot UI state (HC path)
- [ ] Slot choice visible read-only in source detail; no in-place switch
- [ ] `./gradlew testDebugUnitTest` green

## Key Considerations

- Changing the slot must not delete stored rows (family history stays in Room, just
  invisible and unsynced).
- Unique index (timestamp, userSlot, sourceId) keeps re-reads idempotent per slot.

## Anti-Patterns

- No filtering inside Composables; ingestion and queries only.
- No TODOs, no stub implementations.

## Code Map (pre-mapped by investigation, 2026-10-25)

- The seam has NO production reader yet: `SourceReadRequest` is constructed nowhere in main
  code. Build a minimal read orchestrator in this task (e.g. `devices/SourceReadUseCase`):
  ConnectedSource → registry type → `BpSource.read(SourceReadRequest(syncMode, userSlot))`
  → `storeReadings(readings, source.id)` via OmronBpRepository (omron/data/
  OmronBpRepository.kt:46-56; insertIgnore dedups by (timestamp, userSlot, sourceId)).
  Task .5 extends it with modes/anchors; task .6 wires the UI to it.
- The Omron read is ALREADY slot-scoped at protocol level: OmronBleClient.readNewRecords
  (context, key, userSlot, fullRead) reads the per-user EEPROM window; OmronBleSource.read
  (devices/omron/OmronBleSource.kt:44-62) hard-fails on a null request.userSlot. The
  ingestion filter is thus mostly intrinsic — additionally drop non-matching slots
  defensively in the Success mapping (OmronBleSource.kt:53) so a misbehaving device cannot
  leak another user's rows into Room.
- Slot pick UI insertion point: ui/screens/devices/AddSourceFlowScreen.kt PairingContent
  (~:225 — the xlg.3 WIP KDoc marks xlg.4 there); render only when
  SourceTypeOption.supportsUserSlots; write ConnectedSource.userSlot in
  AddSourceViewModel.persist (currently null ~:388-390).
- Slot-scoped DAO exists: allForUser / unsyncedForUser / latest / deleteForUser
  (omron/data/BloodPressureDao.kt:27-80). Add sourceId-scoped variants (allForSource etc.)
  for the future Measurements page; the legacy ui/omron path keeps using the legacy-pref
  slot until task .6 removes it — this transitional dual state is expected, do NOT rewire
  the legacy path.
- Legacy pref to ignore (fresh start): SharedPreferencesOmronSettingsStore user_slot
  (ui/omron/OmronSettingsStore.kt:40-59) — leave untouched; it dies with the legacy UI.
- Read-only slot row target: ui/screens/devices/SourceDetailScreen.kt (xlg.3 WIP).

## Effort Estimate

4 hours

title: Sync modes: History vs Current per source with read anchors
description:
## Goal

Two user-selectable sync modes per device (epic requirement 5): **History** (full device memory
read — backfill everything, idempotent via the unique index) and **Current** (only new
measurements since the last successful read anchor). Exposed in Device Detail.

## Design

- `BpSyncMode { HISTORY, CURRENT }` (defined in T2) stored per source in
  `ConnectedSourceStore` (default HISTORY).
- Semantics in the Omron driver adapter:
  - HISTORY: read the whole ring buffer (all records the device holds), relying on the Room
    unique index (timestamp, userSlot, sourceId) for idempotency.
  - CURRENT: read only records newer than the device's stored last-read anchor
    (position/counters persisted per source in `ConnectedSource`). This formalizes what exists
  today as two separate actions in ui/omron (`OmronBleClient.readNewRecords` for new records
  vs the "Transfer full history" button) into one per-source setting.
- Source Detail: segmented toggle History/Current with one-line explanation of each;
  rendered only for sources whose capabilities include both modes (Health Connect is
  CURRENT-only — no toggle, just an info line).
- Anchor update: only after a successful read+persist (a failed read must not advance the
  anchor — otherwise CURRENT mode silently skips unread records).

## Implementation Checklist

- [ ] HISTORY/CURRENT read behavior in the driver adapter (anchor tracking per device)
- [ ] Anchor persistence in ConnectedDevice + store
- [ ] Mode toggle UI in Device Detail with explanations
- [ ] Strings EN + RU
- [ ] Unit tests (see below)

## Success Criteria

- [ ] CURRENT-mode test: first read returns records, anchor advances; second read with no new
  records returns empty; new record after that => only the new one returned (catches anchor
  advancing on failed reads / re-reading everything)
- [ ] Failed-read test: read throws/fails => anchor unchanged, next read still returns the
  unread records (catches data loss on failure)
- [ ] HISTORY-mode test: full read returns everything every time, re-insert is idempotent by
  unique index (no duplicates in Room)
- [ ] Mode switch persistence test: toggle CURRENT→HISTORY→CURRENT survives store roundtrip
- [ ] `./gradlew testDebugUnitTest` green

## Key Considerations

- Mode applies per source, not global.
- History read of a nearly-full ring buffer can be slow — progress/error states must surface
  (never a silent hang).

## Anti-patterns

- No anchor advance on partial/failed reads.
- No TODOs, no stub implementations.

## Code Map (pre-mapped by investigation, 2026-10-25)

- Read positions live ON THE DEVICE (EEPROM per-user unread counters), not app-side:
  omron/protocol/ReadPlanCalculator.kt — planForUser :27-48 (unread window ≈ CURRENT),
  planFullRing :59-65 (all 100 slots, ignores counters, does NOT reset ≈ HISTORY),
  resetUnreadCounters :72-83. OmronSession.readOut :70-175 drives the session; the counter
  reset write-back @0x0054 happens ONLY when !readFullRing (:132-143).
- KNOWN EDGE to fix here: the counter reset happens MID-SESSION, before session end — a
  failure AFTER the reset write (session end / link drop) discards the in-memory readings
  (omron/ble/OmronBleClient.kt:54-56) while the device anchor already advanced → records
  are lost until a History pass. Mitigation for the orchestrator: after a failed CURRENT
  read, flag the source so the NEXT read falls back to a full-ring plan once (self-healing),
  or preserve partial readings via a Partial result variant. Pick one, test it.
- App-side anchor: ConnectedSource.lastReadAnchor (devices/store/ConnectedSourceStore.kt:40;
  JSON round-trip done) — advance ONLY on Success, inside the read orchestrator built by
  task .4. SourceReadRequest carries no anchor field (devices/api/BpSource.kt:74-77) — the
  device counters remain the real CURRENT anchor for Omron; lastReadAnchor is app-side
  success bookkeeping (and the model for sources without device counters).
- Mode toggle UI: Source Detail screen (xlg.3 WIP) — render only when capabilities include
  both modes (OmronBleSource capabilities :76-80; HcBpSource is CURRENT-only :41-43 — info
  line instead of a toggle).
- Concurrency: no cross-source mutex exists; the orchestrator must serialize reads per
  source (a physical monitor serves one app at a time — OmronGattConnection.kt:99).
- Optional while here: OmronSession.ReadOutResult.skippedRecords is dropped at
  OmronBleClient.kt:53 — consider surfacing through the seam.

## Effort Estimate

4 hours

title: Measurements: single BP page, gated on connected source; absorb Omron dashboard

One single Measurements page (epic requirement 6) for blood-pressure readings, visible ONLY

- [ ] MeasurementsScreen list + status card + empty state
- [ ] Bottom-nav gating on connected devices

## Anti-patterns

## Code Map (pre-mapped by investigation, 2026-10-25)

- Placeholder target: ui/screens/measurements/MeasurementsScreen.kt:18-27 (EmptyState;
  ROUTE_MEASUREMENTS in ui/navigation/AppRoot.kt:45,64,107-109).
- Absorb from ui/omron/DashboardScreen.kt: ReadingRow + MOV/IHB badges (:153-196), state

  exists but is dropped in OmronBpRepository.toDomain :146-155) — surface it.
- Autosync truth: NOT a scheduler — a SharedPreferences flag `auto_sync`
  (ui/omron/OmronSettingsStore.kt:40-60, default true) consumed at

  the same foreground pass. Generalize: add an `autoSync` field (default true) to
  ConnectedSource (devices/store/ConnectedSourceStore.kt:22-38 — no such field yet;
  kotlinx default value keeps old JSON readable) consumed at read time. The ONLY
  WorkManager job in the app is health/SyncWorker (HC pipeline) — do not add another.
- Cross-source query: repository.allForUser(slot) (OmronBpRepository.kt:95-98) is

- Upload engine: BpSyncCoordinator.syncOnce (BpSyncCoordinator.kt:42-69) is slot-scoped and
  reusable per source; markSynced marks all sources' rows (documented, acceptable).
- Drop in this task: OmronActivity (:50-151) + its 3-tab NavHost + the MainActivity
  openOmron entry (MainActivity.kt:107) + manifest entry (AndroidManifest.xml:83);

## Goal

Standard BLE Blood Pressure Service (0x1810) driver — the second BLE source type, covering
dozens of consumer monitors (Beurer, A&D, Microlife, many Omron models). Plugs into the
source seam from task .2 with no core changes.

## Design

New package `devices/ble1810/` + spec doc `docs/ble-1810-protocol.md` (same style as
docs/omron-protocol.md):

- **Scanner**: BLE scan filtered by service UUID 0x1810; already-bonded devices surface
  immediately. Results: `DiscoveredBleDevice(name, address, rssi)`.
- **GATT read session**: connect + system bonding; subscribe indications on Blood Pressure
  Measurement (0x2A35); read Blood Pressure Feature (0x2A49) and Device Information Service
  (0x180A) for the friendly name. Most devices push stored measurements after subscription;
  some require a button press on the device — include an instruction step (like Omron's
  pairing instructions).
- **Measurement parser** (flags field first — verify exact bit numbers against the current
  Bluetooth SIG spec via context7/web during implementation, do not trust memory):
  - units bit: mmHg vs kPa — normalize everything to mmHg.
  - timestamp flag: present => device clock time; absent => read time as record time +
    fingerprint dedup (see below).
  - User ID flag: informational; attribution stays NONE (app owner) per epic R4.
  - Measurement Status bits (body movement, cuff too loose, irregular pulse) — stored as
    flags for badges, same style as Omron MOV/IHB.
- **Fingerprint dedup** for timestamp-less devices: HISTORY re-reads would duplicate rows if
  record time = read time; keep a per-source fingerprint journal (hash of sys/dia/pulse/
  status/relative order) so re-read measurements are recognized, not re-inserted.
- **Session quirks**: indications may arrive before CCCD confirmation; devices push a burst
  then stall — end the session on idle timeout; remove bond when the source is removed.
- **Research findings (2026-10-25, SIG spec + community device reports)**:
  - 0x2A35 is INDICATE (+ CCCD 0x2902), not notify; 0x2A49 Blood Pressure Feature is Read.
  - Filter sentinel failures: SYS/DIA arriving as SFLOAT 0x07FF (2047.0) are failed
    measurements — skip them, never store.
  - Devices self-disconnect after transfer (GATT status 19, remote user terminated) —
    treat as a normal session end, never auto-reconnect in a loop.
  - Transfer semantics vary per model: latest-only / all stored / delete-after-transfer
    (Omron X4 Smart deletes after transfer!) — document the matrix in the spec doc;
    fingerprint dedup keeps re-reads safe either way.
  - userID commonly null/0xFF — confirms NONE attribution (app owner).
  - RACP structured history is rarely implemented — rely on measurement indications only;
    Intermediate Cuff Pressure (0x2A36) is skipped in v1.
  - Verified 0x1810 device families: A&D UA-651BLE, Beurer BM59/BM85, Omron X7/X4/X2
    Smart+ and Bronze BP5150 (standard GATT — unlike the proprietary M-series), boso,
    Silvercrest SBM69, Medisana BU572. NOT over 0x1810: Withings (locked), Microlife
    BP3GY1-2N, Yonker/Yongrow.
- Structure mirrors omron/ble: parser + session state machine pure/fake-able;
  `android.bluetooth` isolated in ONE GATT glue file.

## Implementation Checklist

- [ ] docs/ble-1810-protocol.md (services, characteristics, flags, bonding, quirks)
- [ ] Parser: flags, units, timestamp, user id, status — pure Kotlin
- [ ] Scanner + GATT session (android.bluetooth in one file only)
- [ ] Fingerprint journal for timestamp-less devices
- [ ] Registration in SourceRegistry as "ble-standard-1810"
- [ ] Strings EN + RU (instructions, errors)
- [ ] Unit tests (see below)

## Success Criteria

- [ ] `Ble1810ParserTest`: SIG-spec sample frames — kPa vs mmHg normalization (catches unit
  bug), timestamp present vs absent (catches wrong record time), status flags, a malformed
  or incomplete frame yields an error result, not a crash
- [ ] `Ble1810SessionTest` (faked transport): indication burst => all records stored once;
  re-read does not duplicate (fingerprint journal); idle timeout ends session
- [ ] Registry resolves ble-standard-1810 with no core-class changes
- [ ] Scanner test: non-0x1810 advertisements filtered out
- [ ] `./gradlew testDebugUnitTest` green

## Key Considerations

- Research completed 2026-10-25 and folded into the Design section above — carry those
  findings into docs/ble-1810-protocol.md.
- Real 0x1810 hardware is exercised only in the final verification task (.10) — this task
  verifies via fakes and unit tests.
- Battery: scan stops promptly; indication subscription lives only inside a read session.
- Bonding prompts are system UI — the flow must show an explanatory step before bonding.

## Anti-Patterns

- No `android.bluetooth` imports outside the single GATT glue file.
- No TODOs, no stub implementations.

## Effort Estimate

8 hours

title: Omron BLE: unread counters read from the wrong byte - perpetual 128-record mega-reads
description: Found in the 2026-10-25 post-epic validation. ReadPlanCalculator read the counter from the SECOND byte of each 16-bit field (v0.9 spec transcription of omblepy bits 8-15 as 'high byte'; actually the LOW byte). The 0x8000 reset leaves 0x80 in the second byte -> every transfer after the first planned a 128-slot read (the perpetual '128 measurements transferred'), crossing into the other user's ring and polluting slot-1 storage with USER2 records. Empirically settled: unread field reads 01 00 after one new measurement, 00 80 after reset; fresh record 140/76/66 decoded byte-exact at 0x0D08 (slot 99). Fixed in c2b9b59 (calculator + regression test on raw wire bytes + spec 5.1 correction + ring endpoints 0x0098-0x06D7 / 0x06D8-0x0D17).
