title: Task 3: Pure JVM protocol codecs — frame codec with XOR CRC, record bit-decoder, SFLOAT utility, protocol constants
description: Android-free protocol layer for the Omron BLE core: SessionFrameCodec (build/parse 8-byte command frames and data frames, XOR CRC), RecordDecoder (16-byte bit-packed layout per docs/omron-protocol.md section 6), SFloatDecoder (0x2A35 support, tested but unused by default), OmronProtocol constants file, BloodPressureReading domain record. TDD with vectors from the spec.
design:
## Goal
The Android-free protocol layer of the Omron BLE core exists under
`app/src/main/java/com/zamotkin/extrahealthgarmin/omron/protocol/` (plus the domain record in
`omron/`), fully unit-tested against vectors from docs/omron-protocol.md. No Android imports
anywhere in these files — they compile and test as plain JVM code.

## Context
- Spec: docs/omron-protocol.md v0.9 (commit bbef2fe). Sections 4 (frames/CRC), 5 (memory map),
  6 (record layout) are the requirements source. Constants are `[SRC]`-cited there; the ones
  still `[UNVERIFIED-on-device]` must live ONLY in OmronProtocol.kt so a capture amendment
  touches one file.
- Task 2 (device capture) is open but hardware-blocked; per user decision we proceed without
  the device. Nothing here touches BLE hardware.
- Project conventions: plain JUnit4 (no Robolectric), backtick test names, in-memory fakes,
  one test class per production class under `app/src/test/java/com/zamotkin/extrahealthgarmin/omron/`.

## Implementation (TDD: RED first for each class)
1. `omron/BloodPressureReading.kt` — data class: timestampEpochSec (Long), systolic, diastolic,
   pulse (Int), mov, ihb (Boolean), userSlot (Int, 1 or 2). No Android types.
2. `omron/protocol/OmronProtocol.kt` — object with all protocol constants from spec sections
   1.2/4/5/6: GATT UUIDs (as String constants), session/read/write/end frame types, record
   region addresses, slot sizes, bit ranges, settings addresses, unlock opcodes/responses.
   Header comment: "Constants from docs/omron-protocol.md — amend there first, then here."
3. `omron/protocol/SessionFrameCodec.kt`:
   - buildCommand(type: Int, address: Int, data: ByteArray): ByteArray — size byte, type
     BE, address BE, data length, data, 0x00 pad, XOR CRC last; throws IllegalArgumentException
     on size/address overflow.
   - parseFrame(bytes): ParsedFrame(size, type, address, dataLength, data) — validates XOR
     invariant (XOR of all bytes == 0), throws FrameCrcException on mismatch; supports the
     8f00 status special case (data = 1 status byte).
   - Prebuilt SESSION_START / SESSION_END frames matching spec vectors byte-for-byte.
4. `omron/protocol/RecordDecoder.kt` — decodeRecord(16 bytes, userSlot): BloodPressureReading
   per spec section 6 bit table (little-endian bit numbering, second clamp 59, sys+25);
   returns null for all-0xFF empty slots; throws RecordFormatException on invalid date
   (month/day/hour/minute out of range) — caller skips with log per spec decision log #6.
5. `omron/protocol/SFloatDecoder.kt` — decode(bytes 2, offset): Double per IEEE 11073 SFLOAT
   (12-bit mantissa + 4-bit exponent, both two's complement, LE). Marked in KDoc:
   "0x2A35 support only — NOT used by the EEPROM path."
6. Tests (one class per production class, vectors from the spec):
   - SessionFrameCodecTest: session-start frame equals `08 00 00 00 00 10 00 18` byte-for-byte;
     end frame equals `08 0f 00 00 00 00 00 07`; read command for addr 0x0260 size 0x26 matches
     omblepy example; XOR invariant on random roundtrips (100 seeded cases); CRC corruption
     detected; 8f00 status byte exposed; oversized data throws.
   - RecordDecoderTest: synthetic vector built by hand (e.g. sys byte 120 -> 145 mmHg after
     +25), timestamp roundtrip, second clamp 63->59, all-0xFF -> null, invalid month -> throws,
     mov/ihb flags, both user slots.
   - SFloatDecoderTest: spec example bytes 0x88 0xF4 -> -116.0; positive value; subnormal-ish
     exponent; NaN mantissa pattern (-2048) -> Double.NaN.

## Success Criteria
- [ ] 5 production files, zero Android imports in omron/protocol/ and omron/BloodPressureReading.kt
      (verify: grep -r "android\." on those paths returns nothing)
- [ ] 3 test classes, all vectors traceable to a spec section (cited in test KDoc)
- [ ] ./gradlew testDebugUnitTest --tests "com.zamotkin.extrahealthgarmin.omron.*" passes
- [ ] Spec decision log items #2/#5/#6 enforced by tests (plain-integer decode, FF-skip, second clamp)

## Key Considerations (SRE review)
- Bit indexing trap: spec bit 0 = LSB of byte 0 (little-endian whole-record integer). Implement
  exactly one private bitsToInt(bytes, first, last) helper mirroring omblepy's
  `_bytearrayBitsToInt` and test it against hand-computed vectors — an off-by-one here corrupts
  every medical value silently.
- sys+25 offset: omitting it produces plausible-but-wrong pressures 25 mmHg low — tests MUST
  pin the offset (catches silent data corruption, the worst kind for a medical app).
- IllegalArgumentException vs custom exceptions: parse/record failures use dedicated exception
  types (FrameCrcException, RecordFormatException) so the BLE layer can map them onto
  OmronBleResult without string matching.
- Keep this package free of Android NOW: pulling in android.util.Log would break unit tests on
  this JDK 26 toolchain (Robolectric unavailable) — logging stays in the BLE layer.
- No time-sync or settings-cache logic here (that is task 4, it needs block-write orchestration).

title: Omron BLE: notification callback never fires on Android 13+ (targetSdk 33+) - unlock responses invisible to transport
description: ROOT CAUSE #2 (the real blocker, found 23:10 via instrumentation + btsnoop): OmronGattConnection never calls BluetoothGatt.setCharacteristicNotification(characteristic, true) - the LOCAL client-side subscription. The CCCD write alone makes the device send notifications (btsnoop: every unlock write 01||key16 answered with a 17-byte 8100 notification ~50ms later) but the phone stack does not deliver them to onCharacteristicChanged without the local registration. Symptom chain: descWrite/charWrite callbacks fire, changed never fires (neither overload). MEDM Health on the same phone receives its 2A2B notifications and 2A35 indications fine. Fix #1 (kept, also required): the API-33+ 3-arg onCharacteristicChanged override was missing. Fix #2: add setCharacteristicNotification before each CCCD enable. Both landed on branch omron. Latent (deferred): registration flow spec 3.2 not implemented - the ALRU answered 8100 to plain unlock while never registered.

title: 5: Remediate review findings (token persistence, sync lock, infinity validation)
description:
# Task 5: Remediate Phase-4 review findings (from orchestrator's invariant sweep)

## Goal
Fix the defects found in the manual invariant sweep; re-verify suite green.

## Findings to fix
1. HIGH: Refreshed Garmin tokens are never persisted after upload. GarminAuthClient.refreshIfNeeded/forceRefresh return new GarminTokens (rotated refresh token), GarminUploadClient keeps them local, GarminRepository never saves. Next upload loads stale refresh token -> eventual GarminAuthError -> forced re-login. Fix: persist current tokens in GarminRepository on UploadResult.Success/Partial (and NotNeeded is pre-network, no refresh happened — no save needed). GarminUploadClient cannot persist (no store dependency) — do it in repository after successful call. Test: repository test where fake remote's uploadWeighIns returns after a simulated refresh — assert tokenStore updated (fake remote should model a token swap: expose last tokens received).
2. MEDIUM: Double-sync concurrency gap. startSync guards on in-memory hcSyncRunning (UI process), SyncWorker runs in a separate process pass on the same files. Small window: worker mid-upload + user taps Sync now -> two engine passes interleave -> possible duplicate upload of the same batch (both passes read the same pending set before either persists). Fix: add a process-wide file lock around SyncEngine.sync() (lock file in filesDir with tryLock semantics — non-blocking; if lock held, return SyncResult.Idle). Document: cross-process safety only (same-process already serialized by hcSyncRunning). Test: second concurrent sync returns Idle while first holds lock (use real FileSyncStateStore temp dir).
3. LOW: validateRanges checks isNaN but not isInfinite for weight/bmi/fat/bone/lean/water/BMR fields. An infinite value passes NaN checks, reaches FIT encoder (uint16 cast of infinity). Fix: add isInfinite to each field check. Test: each field with Float.POSITIVE_INFINITY -> GarminValidationError.

## Success Criteria
- [ ] ./gradlew testDebugUnitTest lintDebug assembleDebug green, tests >= 155
- [ ] New tests: token persistence on upload success; sync lock contention -> Idle; infinity rejection per field
- [ ] No behavior change otherwise

## Anti-patterns
- NO redesign of the upload flow; minimal deltas

title: Omron BLE core module: state machine, EEPROM protocol, record decoding
description: Kotlin BLE client for Omron M7 Intelli IT: coroutine state machine, verified session framing + CRC, bit-packed record decoder, encrypted pairing key
design:
## Requirements (IMMUTABLE)
- A new package `omron/` under com.zamotkin.extrahealthgarmin implements the BLE client for Omron M7 Intelli IT (HEM-7361T-ALRU) as a strict sequential state machine with states per docs/omron-protocol.md (verified spec from epic tefal2garmin-ipo): Idle -> Scanning (filter 0x1810) -> Connecting (no autoConnect) -> DiscoveringServices -> Authenticating (SMP bonding + application-level key registration per spec) -> Unlocking (write key to unlock characteristic) -> ReadingSettings (unread-record counter @ per spec) -> ReadingEeprom (session start/read/end frames with CRC) -> Decoding -> Disconnecting (gatt.close() always).
- GATT operations are strictly sequential: the next operation is issued only after the previous one's callback (BluetoothGattCallback) completes. A single GATT-operation queue/serializer (not parallel writes) backs this.
- Record decoding implements the VERIFIED bit layout (16-byte records, sys = bits 120-127 + 25, dia = bits 112-119, pulse = bits 104-111, timestamp bit fields, mov/ihb flags) — NOT the SFLOAT layout from the original docs/omron.md (SFLOAT decoder may be included as a separately tested utility for the 0x2A35 path, clearly marked unused-by-default).
- The 16-byte proprietary session frame (start/read/write/end) with the CRC algorithm from the verified spec is implemented as a pure, unit-testable codec with zero Android dependencies.
- The pairing key is 16 bytes, generated randomly on first pairing (SecureRandom), persisted encrypted via the existing TokenCrypto pattern (Android Keystore AES, separate alias), never logged in release.
- Error handling maps GATT failures (error 133, GATT_INSUFFICIENT_AUTHENTICATION, timeouts) onto a sealed OmronBleResult: BondingRequired, AuthFailed, Timeout(state), Disconnected, Success(records); every non-success path releases the GATT resource.
- All protocol constants (UUIDs, addresses, bit offsets) live in one OmronProtocol.kt file sourced from docs/omron-protocol.md.

## Success Criteria (MUST ALL BE TRUE)
- [ ] Full readout flow works on the real M7 Intelli IT: scan -> pair -> unlock -> read settings -> read EEPROM -> decode >= 1 real measurement matching the device's own display
- [ ] Unit tests cover: session frame codec (hex vectors from the verified spec incl. CRC), record bit-decoder (vectors from hem-7361t.py layout), state machine transitions, error mapping (133, auth, timeout)
- [ ] gatt.close() called on every exit path (verified via fake-GATT test)
- [ ] No secrets in logs (RedactingHttpLogger-equivalent redaction for the key bytes)
- [ ] ./gradlew testDebugUnitTest passes

## Anti-Patterns (FORBIDDEN)
- ❌ NO SFLOAT-based EEPROM decoding (correctness: verified spec says plain bit-packed ints; SFLOAT was the doc's error) — SFLOAT utility only for 0x2A35, marked unused
- ❌ NO parallel GATT operations (BLE requirement: strict callback-serialized sequencing)
- ❌ NO hardcoded pairing key in source (security: omblepy's hardcoded key is a reference smell; generate + encrypt per install)
- ❌ NO BLE logic inside Activity/ViewModel (architecture: coroutines-based suspending client, injected like existing manual wiring)
- ❌ NO autoConnect=true (reliability: omblepy + Android docs — direct connect with explicit retry policy)
- ❌ NO changes to existing health/ or garmin/ packages (isolation: Omron module is additive)

## Approach
Port the verified omblepy wire protocol to Kotlin on Android's native BLE stack (BluetoothLeScanner + BluetoothGatt + BluetoothGattCallback), wrapped in a coroutine-based state machine. Pure protocol codec (frame builder/parser, record decoder) is Android-free for JVM unit tests. Pairing key stored via a new Keystore alias next to the existing DI token alias.

## Architecture
- omron/protocol/OmronProtocol.kt — UUIDs, addresses, bit offsets (from verified spec)
- omron/protocol/SessionFrameCodec.kt — 8-byte command frames + CRC (pure JVM)
- omron/protocol/RecordDecoder.kt — 16-byte record -> BloodPressureReading (pure JVM)
- omron/protocol/SFloatDecoder.kt — 0x2A35 support only (pure JVM, tested, unused by default)
- omron/ble/OmronBleStateMachine.kt — states + transition table
- omron/ble/OmronBleClient.kt — scanner/GATT wrapper, suspending API, gatt.close() on all paths
- omron/ble/OmronKeyStore.kt — EncryptedSharedPreferences/Keystore persistence of the 16-byte key
- omron/BloodPressureReading.kt — domain record (timestamp, sys, dia, pulse, mov, ihb, userSlot)

## Design Rationale
### Problem
The app today syncs weigh-ins only; blood pressure data has no path into Garmin Connect. Direct BLE readout bypasses the closed Omron Connect ecosystem.

### Research Findings
**Codebase:**
- garmin/TokenCrypto.kt — existing Android Keystore AES pattern to reuse for the Omron key
- health/SyncEngine.kt — coroutine-based pass pattern to mirror
- Manual wiring (no DI framework) per CLAUDE.md — OmronBleClient wired in HealthSyncWiring style

**External:**
- omblepy (verified): GATT channel UUIDs, frame types 0000/0100/01c0/0f00, key write flow, per-model config
- Android BLE docs: callback-serialized GATT, error 133 mitigation (fresh Gatt instance, no autoConnect, main-thread callbacks)

### Approaches Considered
#### 1. Native Android BLE + coroutine state machine ✓
Chosen: no extra dependency, matches existing zero-DI/manual-wiring style; state machine gives testability.
#### 2. Nordic BLE library (no.nordicsemi.android:ble) ❌
Nice API but adds a dependency and its own threading model; KISS + existing conventions win.
#### 3. RxAndroidBle ❌
Rx dependency in a coroutines app; inconsistent.

### Scope Boundaries
**In scope:** scan/pair/auth/readout/decode of new records for the selected user slot, suspending API.
**Out of scope:** Room storage (epic 3), UI (epic 4), background/periodic sync via WorkManager (deferred; foreground interactive sync preferred per doc's energy requirement), time sync write (deferred — flag in code).

### Open Questions
- Which RX/TX channel characteristic the M7 uses (4 candidates in omblepy) — resolved at first real connection; log available channels
- Whether bonding must be re-done after Omron Connect re-pair (doc says device supports one app at a time) — document in spec, handle BondingRequired error with user instruction

## Design Discovery (Reference Context)
### Key Decisions Made
| Question | Answer | Implication |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| SFLOAT or plain ints for EEPROM records? | Plain bit-packed ints per omblepy | SFLOAT only as tested-unused utility |
| Pairing key: fixed or generated? | Generated per install, Keystore-encrypted | New alias + key store class |
| BLE library or native? | Native + coroutine state machine | No new deps |
| autoConnect? | Never | Explicit retry policy |
